From e81e36a96bb56f243b5ac1d114c37c086761595b Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Alan Douglas <adouglas@cadence.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Oct 2018 17:15:54 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] PCI: cadence: Write MSI data with 32bits

According to the PCIe specification, although the MSI data is only
16bits, the upper 16bits should be written as 0. Use writel
instead of writew when writing the MSI data to the host.

Fixes: 37dddf14f1ae ("PCI: cadence: Add EndPoint Controller driver for Cadence PCIe controller")
Signed-off-by: Alan Douglas <adouglas@cadence.com>
Signed-off-by: Lorenzo Pieralisi <lorenzo.pieralisi@arm.com>

diff --git a/drivers/pci/controller/pcie-cadence-ep.c b/drivers/pci/controller/pcie-cadence-ep.c
index 6692654798d4..c3a088910f48 100644
--- a/drivers/pci/controller/pcie-cadence-ep.c
+++ b/drivers/pci/controller/pcie-cadence-ep.c
@@ -355,7 +355,7 @@ static int cdns_pcie_ep_send_msi_irq(struct cdns_pcie_ep *ep, u8 fn,
 		ep->irq_pci_addr = (pci_addr & ~pci_addr_mask);
 		ep->irq_pci_fn = fn;
 	}
-	writew(data, ep->irq_cpu_addr + (pci_addr & pci_addr_mask));
+	writel(data, ep->irq_cpu_addr + (pci_addr & pci_addr_mask));
 
 	return 0;
 }
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/pci/controller/pcie-cadence-ep.c`**
   - The line of code that writes the MSI data has been modified:
     - Changed from `writew(data, ep->irq_cpu_addr + (pci_addr & pci_addr_mask));` to `writel(data, ep->irq_cpu_addr + (pci_addr & pci_addr_mask));`
   - This change updates the function to use a 32-bit write operation instead of a 16-bit write operation when writing the MSI data.

### Relationships

- The modification addresses a compliance issue with the PCIe specification, which states that while the MSI data is only 16 bits, the upper 16 bits should be set to zero. By using `writel` instead of `writew`, the patch ensures that the upper 16 bits are correctly written as zero, thus fixing the bug introduced in a previous commit (identified by the hash `37dddf14f1ae`). This change enhances the correctness of the MSI handling in the Cadence PCIe controller driver.
